metadata.title: Integrating Vector Databases across Embedding Models
metadata.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data
metadata.version: Published journal article; distinct from its SIGMOD 2026 presentation. Institutional repository labels the linked PDF an accepted author manuscript.

sources.what_verified: Publisher-deposited journal-article metadata: canonical title, author order, DOI, PACMMOD volume 3 issue 6, pages 1-28, December 2025 publication dates. Input metadata matches.

Author identities and order, integration topic, local-isometry hypothesis, PACMMOD 3(6), article 338, 28 pages, and SIGMOD 2026 event. Its accepted/in-press 23 August 2025 label is repository status, not the final journal publication date.
Lists the same work and author order under SIGMOD 2026; corroborates presentation-year distinction.

sources.access: LIVE GitHub API resolved main to this commit; raw source retrieved live
sources.what_verified: Authors research-group code identifies A2M as global mean-centered Procrustes and LA2M as source-reference k-means with local fits and nearest-centroid routing. Lines 105-126 implement global A2M, cluster fits for >=2 references and singleton global fallback; line 160 includes 20 among sweep settings. This is implementation evidence, not a claim that these choices were all mandated by the original paper.
Repository identifies its LA2M reproduction folder with this SIGMOD work and separately cites the PACMMOD article as year 2025 with presentation at SIGMOD 2026.
No PDF content verified; no inferred section, theorem, original setting, or quantitative claim is attributed to an unread PDF.

uses.reason: The cited A2M/LA2M baseline family is appropriate. Live authors code supports centered global rectangular Procrustes, source-reference clusters, >=2-reference local fits, and global fallback for singletons. Twenty clusters is one supported configuration. The paragraph expressly declares adaptations rather than exact original-setting reproduction. Citation alone does not verify this manuscript implementation or its results; that is outside this per-entry audit.

LA2M is an appropriate source for the local-alignment alternative and global orthogonal alignment context. The claim is qualitative and makes no unsupported numerical or superiority assertion. The neighboring neural-regression claim is assigned to the separate simplelinear citation and is not audited here.

The institutional abstract establishes cross-model vector-database integration via the local-isometry hypothesis. Live author-group code explicitly identifies global A2M and clustered local LA2M, supporting the supplied summary. PDF was inaccessible, so this conclusion relies on abstract plus official implementation rather than unverified full-text detail.

optional_improvement: Optionally add note = {Presented at SIGMOD 2026}; retain year 2025 and journal-article type. This clarification is not required to repair the correct current entry.
